title: Why can't you add yet?
text: To add fractions, the pieces must be the same size. The denominators 4 and 6 are different, so the fractions are not counting the same kind of piece. A common mistake is to add the denominators and answer $$\frac{2}{10}$$. What is the least common denominator: the smallest positive number that both 4 and 6 divide into?

title: Rewrite the first fraction
text: 4 goes into 12 three times, so multiply the numerator and the denominator of $$\frac{1}{4}$$ by 3. What is the new numerator?

title: Rewrite the second fraction
text: 6 goes into 12 two times, so multiply the numerator and the denominator of $$\frac{1}{6}$$ by 2. What is the new numerator?

title: Add the numerators only
text: Both fractions now have denominator 12: $$\frac{3}{12} + \frac{2}{12}$$. Add the numerators and keep 12. What is the numerator of the sum?

title: Worked solution
text: $$\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{12} + \frac{2}{12} = \frac{5}{12}$$. Common mistake: adding denominators to get $$\frac{2}{10}$$. Denominators name the size of the pieces; they are not terms you add. General rule: rewrite both fractions with the least common denominator, add the numerators, and keep that denominator.
